e.etymology: A modern American compound of Ana (from Hebrew Hannah, grace) and Leigh (Old English leah, meadow or clearing); a spelling of Annalee.
e.note: The spelling begins with the letters a-n-a-l, which some readers will notice; Annaleigh avoids it.

e.etymology: The English word for the people of the Netherlands, from Middle Dutch dutsch, of the people. Long an American nickname for boys of Dutch or German descent, it is now given as a first name.
namesakes: Dutch Schultz (New York mobster of the Prohibition era)

assoc.t: Dutch, the people and language of the Netherlands
going Dutch, splitting the bill
Dutch van der Linde, gang leader in Red Dead Redemption
Dutch, Ronald Reagan's lifelong nickname

e.etymology: A modern American name that extends Kain or Kane with the -en ending of Kaiden and Jalen. It also echoes Cainan, a patriarch in the Genesis genealogies of the King James Bible.
A spelling of Jayceon, an American elaboration of Jace and Jason that surged around 2013; rapper The Game was born Jayceon Taylor. Jason is from Greek Iason, linked to iasthai, to heal.
From Sanskrit darsha, sight or seeing, from the root drsh, to see, which also gives Darshan. In the Hindu calendar darsha is also the day of the new moon.
A Japanese girls' name written with many character combinations. The most common joins sa, sand, with ori, weaving or woven cloth.

assoc.t: Saori Kido, the Athena of the anime Saint Seiya

e.etymology: From Sanskrit dhruva, fixed or constant, the word for the pole star. In Hindu tradition the boy prince Dhruva won the star's unmoving place in the sky through his devotion to Vishnu.
A modern coinage in the Zayden and Kaden family, spelled with an X. Its use jumped after 2023 as the name of Xaden Riorson, the dragon rider hero of Rebecca Yarros's novel Fourth Wing.

assoc.t: Xaden Riorson, hero of the novel Fourth Wing

e.meaning: divinely beautiful (as a short form of Astrid)
e.etymology: In Scandinavia a women's name, from Old Norse Ásta, a short form of Ástríðr (Astrid). In the US it is now given mostly to boys, after Asta, the hero of the manga and anime Black Clover.

assoc.t: Asta, hero of the anime and manga Black Clover
Asta, the terrier in the Thin Man films

e.meaning: emperor (the sense the name took on after Julius Caesar)
e.etymology: The family name of Julius Caesar, of unknown origin; Romans linked it to caesaries, a head of hair. His heirs turned it into the emperor's title, the source of kaiser and tsar.

assoc.t: Julius Caesar, Roman general and dictator
Caesar salad
Caesar, ape leader in the Planet of the Apes films
Caesars Palace and Caesars casinos
Little Caesars pizza chain

e.meaning: wealth, fortune; in Hebrew, I will thank God
e.etymology: A form of Odilia or Ottilie, from the Germanic element od, wealth or fortune, borne by Saint Odilia of Alsace. Odelia is also a modern Hebrew name meaning I will thank God.
A respelling of Ariana, the Italian form of Ariadne, the Cretan princess of Greek myth, whose name is read as ari, most, plus adnos, holy.

assoc.t: Ariana Grande, pop star (same sound)

e.etymology: A modern American name in the family of Kalen, Caelan and Callan. Those spellings are often traced to Gaelic Cailean (Colin) or Irish Caolán, slender, but Calen has no single settled source.
Several names share this spelling: Hebrew Adi, jewel or ornament, used for both sexes in Israel; Sanskrit adi, first or beginning; and a short form of Aditya, Adrian, Adelaide and other Ad- names.
A J spelling of Gentry, an English surname and word for people of good birth, from Old French genterie, nobility.
A modern American name that joins the Ry- of Riley and Ryan to the -lyn ending; a feminine-leaning spelling of Rylan.
A respelling of Jason shaped by Jay and Jace. Jason comes from Greek Iason, linked to iasthai, to heal, and was the name of the leader of the Argonauts.
From Sanskrit adi, first or beginning. Also a short form of Aditya and other Indian names in Adi-; the double a marks the long vowel.

e.meaning: beauty, in most spellings; yumi is also the Japanese bow
e.etymology: A Japanese name usually written with mi, beauty, after a first character such as reason, abundance or gentleness; the word yumi also means an archery bow. Yumi is used in Korea as well.

assoc.t: Yumi of the cartoon Hi Hi Puffy AmiYumi

e.etymology: A respelling of Camila, the Spanish and Portuguese form of Latin Camilla, from camillus, a noble youth who assisted at religious rites. Virgil gave the name to a warrior maiden in the Aeneid.
Used in Latin America as a feminine form of Dariel, a modern name often linked to Darío.
From Greek Lysandros, built from lysis, release, and aner, man. It was the name of the Spartan admiral who won the Peloponnesian War, and of a young lover in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
namesakes: Lysander (Spartan admiral who defeated Athens in 404 BC)

assoc.t: Lysander, lover in A Midsummer Night's Dream

e.etymology: The English word for a woman who inherits wealth or a title, from heir (Latin heres) plus -ess. Its use as a name grew after rapper T.I. and Tameka Harris named their daughter Heiress in 2016.

assoc.t: heiress, the word for a woman who inherits a fortune

e.etymology: A spelling of Jody, which began as a pet form of Judith (Hebrew Yehudit, woman of Judea) by way of Judy, and for boys as a pet form of Joseph or Jude.
namesakes: Jodie Foster (Oscar-winning star of The Silence of the Lambs)
Jodie Comer (Emmy-winning star of Killing Eve)
Jodie Sweetin (Stephanie Tanner on Full House)

assoc.t: Jodie Foster, actress and director

e.meaning: the Cheyenne people of the Great Plains
e.etymology: A phonetic respelling of Cheyenne, the name of a Great Plains nation and of Wyoming's capital. Cheyenne comes from Šahíyena, the Dakota name for that people.

assoc.t: Cheyenne, the capital of Wyoming (same sound)
the Cheyenne, a Great Plains nation (same sound)

e.etymology: A spelling of Donovan, an Irish surname from Ó Donnabháin, descendant of Donndubhán, a byname joining donn, brown, and dubh, dark.
From Greek Nikolaos, nike, victory, plus laos, people. Nicola is the everyday Italian form of Nicholas for men, while in Britain it has been a women's name since the 20th century.
e.note: In the US it is given mostly to boys; in Britain and Ireland Nicola is almost always a woman's name.

e.etymology: A spelling that sits between Elissa and Alyssa. Elissa is the Greek form of the Phoenician name of Dido, queen of Carthage, and also a short form of Elisabeth; Alyssa is a 20th-century relative of Alicia.

A spelling of Delilah without the final h, as in German and Dutch. Hebrew Delilah is tied to a root meaning to weaken or languish; in the Book of Judges she coaxes out the secret of Samson's strength.

assoc.t: Delilah, who betrays Samson in the Bible
Hey There Delilah, 2006 hit by the Plain White T's

e.note: The biblical Delilah betrayed Samson, so the name once implied a temptress; few hear it that way now.

e.etymology: A respelling of Isabella that writes in the nickname Izzy. Isabella is the Latinate form of Isabel, the medieval Spanish and Occitan form of Elizabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath.
An Irish surname, from Mac Thighearnáin, son of Tighearnán, a personal name formed from tighearna, lord, with a diminutive ending.
namesakes: Kiernan Shipka (Sally Draper on Mad Men, star of Chilling Adventures of Sabrina)

e.etymology: The Italian short form of Alessandro (Alexander), from Greek alexein, to defend, and aner, man. It is also a pet form of Aleksandre in Georgia.
namesakes: Sandro Botticelli (Renaissance painter of The Birth of Venus)

assoc.t: Sandro, French fashion label
